newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo plans $1.5 bln French investment.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo plans $1.5 bln French investment.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Electronics Co plans to invest $1.5 billion to make electronic parts in France, creating 5,000 new jobs, company chairman Bae Soon-hoon said on Thursday.
"We plan to invest $1.5 billion in France by the year 2000 to produce electronic parts such as glass bulbs for TV picture tubes," Bae told a news conference.
"The investment is expected to create about 5,000 jobs there," Bae told a news conference.

Bae's remarks came a day after the French government announced it planned to sell the state-owned defence and consumer electronics group Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe Lagardere in turn will sell consumer electronics maker Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo.
The French prime minister's office said Daewoo's offer entailed a commitment to preserve Thomson Multimedia jobs in France and create additional jobs.
"Employment is a big issue in France and we will do our utmost to create new jobs there with steady investment," Bae said.
"All the French jobs at Thomson will be preserved and we will focus on cutting production costs by 10 percent for the normalisation of operations," he said.
Bae said Daewoo forecast demand for an extra 1.5 million television sets over its current production by 2000. Output last year was 6.5 million sets.
"If we utilise Thomson's facilities, no layoffs at all will occur at the company," he said.
The French government has said it will take a final decision on the Thomson sale after studying the privatisation commission's conclusions and legal opinion.

France's independent privatisation commission, which has an important say in the sale of state assets, still has to give its advice on the sale, but it is unlikely to overturn the government's own decision.
Bae said the purchase of Thomson Multimedia would make Daewoo the world's largest television maker. Thomson produces about eight million sets a year, Bae said.
He said Daewoo wanted Thomson to retain all its own brand name products in the United States, but to cut the number marketed in Europe to about two.
He dismissed suggestions that Daewoo's purchase of Thomson Multimedia could pose difficulties for the management of Daewoo.
"I don't think it is an ailing company, even though I see some room for improvement in efficiency," Bae said.

He said he would become chief executive of Thomson Multimedia, which posted a 1.09 billion franc ($209.3 million) net loss in calendar 1995 on 36.5 billion franc turnover, according to a statement from Daewoo.
Television sets accounted for 42 percent of Thomson Multimedia's 1995 sales, followed by video-cassette recorders and TV picture tubes that each made up 15 percent of sales, the statement said.

Daewoo Electronics, a unit of the Daewoo Group, posted a net profit of 47.2 billion won ($57 million) in calendar 1995 on turnover of 3.13 trillion won, compared with 34.8 billion profit on 2.5 trillion won turnover.
Daewoo operates three production plants in France, with a total investment of $182 million, making microwave ovens, colour TVs and picture tubes.
(Conversion: $1= 828 won, $1= 5.208 French francs)
